title: Electromagnetic Spectrum
seo_title: Secondary 3 Physics: Electromagnetic Spectrum Worksheets (O-Level 6091 with Answers)
standard_text: State that all electromagnetic waves are transverse, travel with the same high speed of 3.0 × 10⁸ m/s in a vacuum and transfer energy; describe the main components of the electromagnetic spectrum in order of wavelength and frequency; describe typical uses of each region (radio and television, satellite and mobile communication, remote controls and thermal imaging, optical fibres, sterilisation, X-ray imaging and radiotherapy); describe the harmful effects of over-exposure and how to reduce them (summary of the Singapore-Cambridge O-Level Physics 6091 syllabus).
meta_desc: Free Secondary 3 O-Level Physics worksheets on the electromagnetic spectrum: properties of EM waves, the order of the spectrum, uses and dangers of radio, microwaves, infrared, light, UV, X-rays and gamma rays. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: All EM waves travel at 3.0 × 10⁸ m/s in a vacuum.
key_sub: Radio, micro, IR, visible, UV, X-ray, gamma: frequency rises.
body_html:
How to think about it

Electromagnetic waves are transverse waves that travel at 3.0 × 10⁸ m/s in a vacuum.

  • In order of increasing frequency (decreasing wavelength): radio waves, microwaves, infrared, visible light, ultraviolet, X-rays, gamma rays.
  • Higher frequency means more energy: UV, X-rays and gamma rays can damage cells and cause cancer.
  • v = fλ also works for light, with v = 3.0 × 10⁸ m/s.
Example

Which has a shorter wavelength: infrared or ultraviolet?

UV is further along the order

Answer: ultraviolet

Example

A microwave has f = 1.0 × 10¹⁰ Hz. Wavelength?

λ = 3.0 × 10⁸ ÷ 1.0 × 10¹⁰

Answer: 0.030 m

Common mistakes

  • Thinking higher-frequency waves travel faster. All EM waves have the same speed in a vacuum.
  • Calling radio waves sound waves. They are electromagnetic.
  • Getting the order of ultraviolet and infrared the wrong way round.
  • Thinking all EM radiation is dangerous. Radio waves and visible light are low-energy.

faq.q: What is the order of the electromagnetic spectrum?
faq.a: Radio waves, microwaves, infrared, visible light, ultraviolet, X-rays and gamma rays, in order of increasing frequency and decreasing wavelength.

faq.q: What do all electromagnetic waves have in common?
faq.a: They are transverse, transfer energy, need no medium and travel at 3.0 × 10⁸ m/s in a vacuum.
Ultraviolet, X-rays and gamma rays carry enough energy to damage cells; high-power microwaves and infrared can heat and burn tissue.
